messages:
jason_customer: Hey team — we started getting 429s across multiple endpoints after a short traffic spike this morning. Burst credits went to 0 in ~3 minutes. App id: acct_99XX. We rely on short bursts; is there a way to avoid this moving forward?

sara_support: Thanks Jason. Can you paste a small snippet of the failing request/response headers (esp any X-*-Burst or Retry-After headers)? Also which API surface (chat/generate/embeddings) and model?

jason_customer: It's chat generation to gpt-redwood-xl, mostly user-initiated flows. Example header we saw: 
```
X-RW-Burst-Credits: 0
X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 12
```
Requests were ~10 req/s for ~3 minutes during the spike.

maria_prod_eng: Quick note on terms — burst credits are a short reserve to absorb spikes but they regen slowly (configurable per plan). If the incoming qps exceeds the regen + baseline for the window, you'll see throttles.

alex_support: Short-term fixes: 1) implement client-side smoothing (token/bucket leaky-bucket) to avoid sending full spike instantly; 2) reduce request sizes or split into smaller chunks; 3) add retries with exponential backoff + jitter. We can also provision a temporary uplift while infra investigates.

jason_customer: Do you have a small repro I can run locally to simulate?

sara_support: Yep — you can hammer a single endpoint with curl to see burst die-off. Example: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate &
done
```
Watch response headers; once X-RW-Burst-Credits hits 0 you'll see Retry-After and 429s.

alex_support: And a recommended client retry skeleton: 
```
async function callWithBackoff(fetchFn) {
  let base = 200; // ms
  for (let i=0;i<6;i++) {
    const res = await fetchFn();
    if (res.status === 200) return res;
    const ra = res.headers.get('Retry-After');
    const wait = ra ? (parseInt(ra)*1000) : (base * Math.pow(2,i) + Math.floor(Math.random()*100));
    await sleep(wait);
  }
  throw new Error('failed after retries');
}
```
This reduces tight retried bursts that make the situation worse.

maria_prod_eng: From the platform side we can: 1) review your regen rate and smoothing policy for acct_99XX; 2) enable per-org gradual recovery (instead of immediate hard cap) as an interim; 3) add alerting on "burst_credit_level" to notify before depletion. I'll open a ticket to SRE.

jason_customer: Temporary uplift would be great — spikes are expected in weekly batch job. Also what's the best metric to watch in our dashboard to preempt?

sara_support: Watch "burst_credit_level" and "throttled_count" and set a dashboard alarm for burst_credit_level < 30% over 5m. Also monitor "requests_per_second" and percentile latency to see if batching is helpful.

alex_support: For medium-term: consider Reserved Capacity (Dedicated) if you need predictable steady throughput, or configure smoothing on the client to align to regen rate (we can share recommended regen numbers for your plan).

devops_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5543 — investigating burst policy for acct_99XX. Assigned to eng-sre.

maria_prod_eng: Follow-up action: I'll DM SRE and request temporary +20% burst quota for next 48h while we add alarms and advise on client smoothing. If you can share exact peak qps and average tokens per request, we can recommend concrete regen_rate.

jason_customer: Peak was ~12 req/s, avg ~350 tokens per chat. Thanks — will DM those details. Appreciate quick help :thumbsup:
